title: The shared interpretive code is constitutional-tier system material
subject: interpretive-code
ratio:
Serenissima maintains the interpretive code that governs how a recorded ratio is read as an
explicit, versioned system artifact identical for all sessions, not composed ad hoc and privately
by each interpreter: translation rules stating how to read a ratio (literal first, then
purposive, then systematic), preference rules ranking competing readings, and procedure rules
fixing the order of application, each rule carrying a stable `IC-NN` id inside a document
(`INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md`) that itself carries an explicit `Version:` line. Every interpretive act
recorded in the registry cites the code version it applied (`interpretive_code_version`), so that
when two sessions disagree, the disagreement decomposes into one of three distinguishable failure
modes -- a different disposition read, a different code version cited, or the same code version
applied differently -- instead of one undifferentiated fog. The code is constitutional-tier
material: amendable only through the overruling-grade protocol, at tier 1 or 2, naming the rules
changed and the version bump; an ordinary edit to the document without a published amending
record is invalid.
scope_conditions: every interpretive act recorded in the registry
revisit_trigger: Revisit at any Version bump of INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md
validity_conditions: INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md declares exactly one line matching Version: v-digit
